Container.Name: dropwatch
Container.Overview:
Dropwatch earns Twitch Drops for you in the background and claims each reward as soon as it's earned.
**What it does** - Picks which campaign to watch, and moves to another channel when a stream goes offline - Collects channel points and watch-streak bonuses on your favourite channels - Lists anything that needs you, such as a game account to link - Web dashboard for priorities, skipped games, pinned campaigns and history, phone included - Optional notifications to Discord, Telegram, ntfy, Slack, Pushover, Gotify or any webhook
**Getting started** Open the WebUI, choose a page password, then sign in to Twitch with a one-time code. One Twitch account per container.
Container.Changes: ### 0.1.1 (2026-10-11) - First release in Community Applications, published by KernelPanic Studios. - Mines Twitch Drops in the background and claims each reward as soon as it's earned. - Collects channel points and watch-streak bonuses on favourite channels. - Web dashboard: what's being mined, what's next, priorities, history and a phone layout. - Needs you: campaigns that need a game account linked, with an Ignore option. - Notifications to Discord, Telegram, ntfy, Slack, Pushover, Gotify or any webhook. - Backup and restore of lists and settings.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Where Dropwatch keeps its database (Twitch sign-in, lists, history) and cached images.

Config.Name: Web UI Port
Config.Description: Port for the Dropwatch web UI.

Config.Name: Allowed host names
Config.Description: Only needed to open Dropwatch through a public domain name, such as a reverse proxy (dropwatch.example.com). Comma-separated. IP addresses and local names like tower or tower.local always work.

Config.Name: Reverse proxy address
Config.Description: Only behind a reverse proxy: its address, so the login lockout sees each visitor's own address.
